subject: Pilot kickoff: Aegis Retail - initial scope, success metrics & access
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aegisretail.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post‑call: discovery recap & pilot ask

Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful conversation. Quick recap from our side and what we’d like to run as a pilot: 

Pain points we articulated on the call:
- Search relevance is inconsistent for long-tail SKUs (many queries return poor or stale results).
- Peak-time latency spikes on product suggestions (search throttles at 99th pct).
- Duplicate/near-duplicate SKUs leading to poor recommendations and higher return rates.

Goals for a 30‑day POC:
- Improve search/recommendation precision for long-tail queries (+10% CTR to PDP).
- Reduce 99th percentile inference latency from ~1.2s to <600ms for the targeted workload.
- Reduce returns caused by relevance issues by ~15%.

Scope we’re proposing (from internal ops):
- Ingest a 30‑day sample of clickstream + product catalog + returns (S3).
- Run a search reranking + suggestion model against a daily eval set.
- Share conversion & return metrics with Redwood for weekly readouts.

Access & data items we can provide right away:
- S3 sample: s3://aegis-retail/pilot-samples/2025-06/ (we can create a cross-account role)
- Example queries + labeled relevance set (CSV attached)
- Network: we can allowlist IPs and open a peering request if needed

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm which model variants you recommend for search reranking (latency vs quality tradeoffs)?
2) What operational access do you need (role ARN, IP ranges, service account)?
3) How quickly can you onboard — target start is July 21 if that works for you.

Attachment: aegis-data-sample.csv (CSV, 2.3 MB)

-Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Search & Personalization | Aegis Retail
jordan.price@aegisretail.com
+1 (415) 555‑0198

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aegisretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post‑call: discovery recap & pilot ask

Jordan — great to connect this morning. Appreciate the clear problem framing. Below is Redwood’s proposed kickoff plan and immediate asks so we can hit your July 21 target.

Proposed pilot scope (30 days):
- Phase 0 (3 days): Access & baseline — we’ll validate data, run a baseline eval on your sample queries, confirm infra plan.
- Phase 1 (14 days): Model + prompt tuning — deploy a lightweight reranker + suggestion generator, iterate prompt set and small quantized variants to hit latency targets.
- Phase 2 (10 days): A/B evaluation + production smoke — holdback traffic experiment and weekly metric review.

Success metrics (what we’ll track):
- Primary: delta in CTR -> PDP on prioritized long‑tail query set (+10% target)
- Secondary: 99th percentile latency (target <600ms) and return rate lift (-15% target)
- Qualitative: manual review of highest‑impact query clusters and failure modes

Owners & contacts:
- Redwood: Olga Petrov (you’re my main point) — technical onboarding and evaluation strategy
- Redwood Ops: Ben Carter — infra, networking, access, and SLA discussion
- Aegis: Jordan Price — product/metrics lead; Samir Khan (you mentioned) for data access and procurement

Immediate access we need (please provision by EOD July 17):
1) Cross-account IAM role ARN with GetObject/ListObject permissions for s3://aegis-retail/pilot-samples/2025-06/ (we’ll use role assumption)
2) Service account email for API key provisioning and an allowlist CIDR for a static egress IP if you prefer (we can do peering instead)
3) A sample of labeled queries + the evaluation rubric (CSV is perfect)

Tech/ops notes:
- Recommended starting model: a mid-sized open encoder‑decoder reranker we can quantize; we’ll benchmark 3 variants (faster small quantized, balanced, high‑quality) and present latency/cost tradeoffs by Day 4.
- We’ll enable prefix caching for repeated query sessions and configure batching so online P99 stays <600ms where possible.

Next steps / calendar items:
- Please confirm access items above by Friday 2025‑07‑17.
- I’ll set a 30‑minute kickoff for July 21 — propose 10:00am PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite with agenda and pre‑read.

Attachment: pilot_summary_olga_v1.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)

Thanks — we’re excited to get this rolling.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
(650) 555‑0122

Jordan / Olga — looping in ops details from my side.

Operational checklist (what we’ll set up on our end):
- Environment: we’ll provision a dedicated test tenant for Aegis on a shared GPU pool unless you prefer dedicated capacity (we can estimate cost).
- Networking: if you choose VPC peering, lead time is ~7 business days for peering + security review. IP allowlisting is faster (same‑day for ranges we publish).
- Monitoring: we’ll enable per‑route latency and token cost dashboards for the pilot and set up automatic alerts for P99 breaches.

Data & eval requests (concrete):
- Labeled eval CSV (query, gold_id, relevance_score) — we’ll need at least 10k rows for a stable baseline.
- 2 weeks of clickstream + catalogue snapshots for cold-start analysis (compressed S3 prefixes are fine).

Prompt/eval artifacts we’ll deliver:
- Baseline eval report (Day 3)
- Prompt set v1 (10–15 anchors) and traffic split plan for A/B (Day 7)
- Weekly readout deck template (we’ll share)

Attaching the network checklist and our standard sandbox access doc for your infra team to review.

Attachments: network_access_instructions.pdf (PDF, 98 KB)

Cost note: rough spend estimate for a 30‑day pilot on shared pool + monitoring is ~$6–9k (final depends on traffic and chosen model variant). If Aegis prefers Dedicated to hit strict SLOs, I can pull a formal quote.

I’ll propose a 30‑minute kickoff invite for July 21 at 10:00am PT — Olga, feel free to send.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
